main_reasons: A $5.46M gain on extinguishment was booked on Dec 30, 2025, when the $7.5M Cooley legal-fee payable was settled for $2.0M cash plus contingent payments of up to $5.5M called 'remote'. ASC 470-60-35-10 generally bars a gain while contingent payments could make up the difference, so this gain looks aggressive or wrong

Without that year-end gain, stockholders' equity of $2.76M would be negative. That is just $265K over Nasdaq's $2.5M Equity Rule threshold, which compliance the company says it regained 'as of December 31, 2025', a strong incentive to manage earnings

Material weakness in long-lived asset impairment: a $1.5M building impairment was an audit adjustment. The remaining $16.6M asset group, including $12.0M of stalled construction-in-progress with mechanics liens, foreclosure suits and a lender cure demand, looks under-impaired; more impairment would push equity below the Nasdaq minimum

The audit committee is running an internal investigation into the root cause of the material weakness. Earlier material weaknesses are also referenced, and a $1.3M business-email-compromise loss in 2024 points to weak controls
Auditor changed in Sept 2024 (Grant Thornton dismissed, Crowe engaged). The thin finance function relies on an interim controller and outside technical advisors
Going-concern doubt with $2.0M cash, $13.1M of past-due payables, the bank loan in discretionary default and a sub-$1 share price after a 1-for-40 reverse split

Complex Level 3 and related-party equity accounting (TDR gains with insiders credited to APIC, $14.3M deemed dividends, the fair-value election for Wugen shares and the contingent liability) leaves room for judgment

Sloppy, inconsistent disclosures, for example the Cooley financing trigger given as $4.0M in one place and $6.0M in another, 'Global Select' vs 'Capital Market', and 'consolidated' statements for a single entity
